transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Um... work, mostly. They... well, I guess I scared everyone at work. I just... I started freezing up in the middle of service. Or doing things out of order. Like... I'd just be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and... I was just repeating table numbers instead of closing out the checks. So... they wanted me to come here.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled by someone else, or heard voices that others don't hear?

Um... no one controls my thoughts. But... I guess... sometimes I hear things. 

Just... a woman's voice. Usually when I'm closing up at work, or... if I'm at home in the kitchen. She just... says my name. Or tells me I'm doing the count wrong. It sounds so real that I actually answer her out loud... before I realize nobody else heard it. 

I don't really like talking about it.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something was true that others didn't seem to understand or agree with, even though you felt certain about it?

Um... I guess. Just... at work. 

I know a couple of the other servers, and... this one regular customer... I know they're watching how I ring things in. They leave these little signs on the tickets. To prove they're trying to get me fired. 

My husband says I'm wrong... he says it's just normal restaurant mess-ups. But... I know what they're doing. I'd rather not get into it, though.
Have you ever felt like things in your environment—like signs, comments, or events—were specifically directed at you or meant to send you a hidden message?

Um... yeah, I guess I just mentioned that. The tickets. 

Like I said... I just know they leave little signs on them. The other servers, and that one regular. It's... it's just little things on the receipts, or how they write them. To... to show they're watching me ring things in. Trying to get me fired. 

My husband says it's just normal mistakes, but... I don't know. I just know what I see. I don't really want to talk about them anymore.
Can you tell me more about how you know the signs on the tickets are meant for you? Do you feel like you're figuring it out on your own, or do you feel like someone is helping you understand them?

I... I just figure it out myself. I already told you about it. 

I just... I look at the tickets, and I can tell. The way the servers write things, or... that regular customer. It's just obvious they're watching me ring things in. They leave those little signs to prove they're trying to get me fired. 

My husband keeps saying it's just normal mess-ups, but... he's not there. I am. I don't... I don't know why we have to keep going over this. I just know it's happening.
How long have you been experiencing these things, like hearing the voice and seeing signs on the tickets?

Um... I don't know exactly. A few months, I guess. 

Maybe... about four months since I really started noticing the tickets and... and being sure about what they're doing. And the voice getting clearer. Since then, mostly.
Outside of work, have you ever experienced any strange thoughts, beliefs, or perceptions that others don't seem to share, even when you were certain they were true?
No. Just... just at work. That's it.
Have you ever experienced any strange thoughts, voices, or perceptions when you’re not at work—like hearing voices or seeing things that others don’t seem to notice?

I... well, I guess sometimes when I'm home. Just in the kitchen. 

I'll hear... a woman. She says my name, or tells me I'm doing the count wrong. It's clear enough that I actually answer her out loud. But then I realize no one else heard it. So... I guess it happens at home sometimes too. But it's still mostly just... work stuff.
When you hear the woman's voice at home, do you ever feel like it's part of something bigger—like it's trying to warn you about something or communicating a special message just for you?

Um... no. I don't think so. 

She just... she just talks about the counting. I don't know about any special messages or... warnings or anything like that. It's just what I told you.

Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts, beliefs, or perceptions in places other than work—like at home or elsewhere in your daily life—where you felt certain something was happening that others didn’t seem to notice?
I... I thought we just talked about this. It's just the kitchen. The voice about the counting. That's... that's all there is. I don't know what else you're looking for.

Have you noticed any other strange or unusual thoughts or beliefs outside of work—like in your home or other places—that make you feel like something is happening that others don’t seem to notice, even if you can’t explain it fully?
I... I really don't know why you keep asking me the same thing. I already told you. It's just the kitchen. There's nothing else. I just... I don't have anything else to tell you.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions outside of work that others don’t seem to understand or agree with, even if you felt certain they were true?

I... I don't know. Like I said, it's just the kitchen. I don't... I don't have these other things you're asking about. People just don't understand the counting, that's all. I don't really have anything else to say about it.
When you hear the woman's voice in the kitchen talking about the counting, do you feel like it's coming from outside of you, or do you feel like it's a part of your own thoughts?

It's... outside. It doesn't feel like a thought. Like I said, it happens when I'm closing up at work, or... or just in my kitchen at home. She'll say my name, or tell me I'm doing the count wrong. It's clear. I usually... I've answered her back before. Just out loud. Before I realize that nobody else heard it.

Have you ever experienced any strange thoughts, voices, or perceptions in places other than work or home—like in public or other locations—where you felt something was happening that others didn’t seem to notice?
No... not out in public. It's really just... what I already told you. At work, and in my kitchen. I don't... I haven't noticed anything anywhere else.
Do you ever feel like the woman's voice in the kitchen is part of a larger plan or connected to something more serious, like a conspiracy or a mission that you're involved in?
No... nothing like that. I don't know what you mean by a mission. It's just... she just talks about the counting. There's no plan or anything. It's just exactly what I already told you.

Outside of work and your kitchen, have you ever had any strong beliefs or suspicions that something strange was happening—like someone watching you, plotting against you, or sending you messages—where you felt certain it was true, even if others didn’t agree?

I mean... not out in public, no. But... at work, sometimes. I just... I feel like some of the other servers, and this one guy who comes in a lot, are... watching me. Like they're paying too much attention to how I ring in orders. Sometimes there are these... little signs on the tickets. Like they're trying to set it up so I get fired. My husband says it's just normal mistakes, but... I don't know. It feels like they're doing it on purpose.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions—like someone watching you or leaving messages—that happened outside of work and home, even if just for a short time?
I... no. I already said, it's just work and home. I don't... I don't know why you keep asking about other places. I just go to work and come home. That's it.

Have you ever had any beliefs or thoughts where you felt completely certain about something that others around you didn’t seem to understand or agree with — even if it wasn’t related to work or the counting you mentioned?
No. I... I really don't. Just the things we already talked about. I don't... I don't have any other thoughts like that. I don't know what else to tell you.
Have you ever had any experiences in other places—like stores, on the street, or anywhere else—where you felt like something strange was happening that others didn’t seem to notice?
I... no. I don't go out much anyway. Just... just home and work. I don't notice anything anywhere else.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms are primarily limited to work and home environments, involving auditory hallucinations (hearing a woman's voice) and delusional beliefs (e.g., being watched, signs on tickets). There is no evidence of a broader, more pervasive psychotic process or mood disturbance. The clinical picture most closely aligns with F23.0 (Acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia) as the symptoms are of acute onset, polymorphic presentation, and without clear thought disorder or negative symptoms characteristic of schizophrenia.
